recreation_brief: 1. Set the slide background to solid light gray (#E8E8E8). 2. Draw a thin horizontal red (#C00000) rule (flat rectangle, ~1% of slide height) spanning the full slide width along the very top edge (0-2% height band), just above the title. 3. Place the title 'How many filters we should apply' horizontally centered in the top band (~2-14% height, ~20-80% width): bold sans-serif (Arial-like), dark red #C00000, ~36pt, sentence case. 4. Insert one rectangle with white (#FFFFFF) fill and a thin blue (#3333CC) border at ~6-94% width and ~16-55% height (upper-middle). Fill it with serif (Times New Roman-like) black (#000000) text, exactly these lines in order: bold header 'Hypothesis'; 'Natural images are stationary'; 'Visual features are common for different parts of one or multiple image'; one blank line; bold header 'Conclusion'; 'It is not required to use different filters for different spatial locations  in the image' (preserve the double space after 'locations'); '(in other words, apply same filter for ALL positions in the image)' — within this line render the run 'apply same filter for ALL positions in the image' as bold sans-serif dark red (#C00000) on a solid yellow (#FFFF00) highlight, with the two parentheses in regular black. 5. Place the left photo at ~18-45% width and ~57-84% height (lower-middle left): the Grumpy Cat meme image (white cat, blue eyes, lying on a gray-blue #8A9BA8 blanket) with bold white (#FFFFFF) sans-serif meme captions with dark outline — 'I LOVE MATH' at the top and 'IT MAKES PEOPLE CRY!' at the bottom — framed by a thin red (#FF0000) border. Overlay exactly 5 detection rectangles: 2 small red (#FF0000) rectangles on the cat's ears (upper-left and upper-right of the head), 1 yellow (#FFFF00) rectangle around the nose/muzzle center, and 2 green (#00CC00) rectangles on the left side near the blanket edge. 6. Place the right photo at ~48-76% width and ~57-84% height (lower-middle right): a small fluffy white-and-tan (#C8B49A) dog lying in a dark brown (#5B3A1E) leather armchair with a warm indoor background, framed by a thin red (#FF0000) border. Overlay exactly 4 detection rectangles: 1 red (#FF0000) rectangle on the dog's ear/head, 1 yellow (#FFFF00) rectangle around the nose, and 2 overlapping green (#00CC00) rectangles on the right side near the chair edge. 7. Insert the bottom annotation rectangle at ~6-94% width and ~86-97% height: light-yellow (#FFFFE1) fill, thin blue (#3333CC) border, containing exactly 3 lines of small italic sans-serif blue (#3333CC) text: line 1 'Apply Red filter to detect ears in the whole image (not necessarily in the middle of the image)' with the word 'Red' colored red (#FF0000); line 2 'Apply filter to detect nose in the whole image' with a blank space between 'Apply' and 'filter' given a solid yellow (#FFFF00) highlight (the filter word is intentionally blank in the source); line 3 'Apply Green filter to detect edges in the whole image' with the word 'Green' colored green (#008000). 8. Do NOT add the solid black strip at the very bottom edge (it is the video-player bar, not slide content) and do NOT add the white mouse-cursor arrow near the right edge of the left photo (live-capture artifact).

fixes_applied: Added the missing layout region 'Top red rule' (thin #C00000 horizontal rule, ~0-2% height, full width): it was described in layout.arrangement and visual_elements but was absent from layout.regions, breaking region coverage.

Replaced the vague phrase 'spanning nearly full width' in layout.arrangement with the exact measure '~6-94% of slide width' taken from layout.regions, and added exact percentage bands for the two photos and the annotation box in the arrangement string.

Rewrote recreation_brief as an 8-step ordered checklist; every step now places exactly one element with exact text, position percentages, hex colors, and shape type; detection-rectangle counts made explicit (left photo: 2 red + 1 yellow + 2 green = 5 rectangles; right photo: 1 red + 1 yellow + 2 green = 4 rectangles).
Replaced the title font-size range '~36-40pt' with the single actionable value '~36pt'.

Changed the final brief step from 'optionally add a solid black strip' to an explicit exclusion: the bottom black bar is the video-player bar and the white mouse cursor is a live-capture artifact — neither is slide content (consistent with their own descriptions in visual_elements).
subtitle_or_header kept null after verification: no subtitle or secondary header exists anywhere in the source JSON; the red title is the only header element.
Preserved the verbatim double space in 'different spatial locations  in the image' and flagged it in the brief so the builder does not 'correct' it.
uncertain_items: Exact point sizes are estimates: the source gives only 'large' for the title (~36pt assumed) and 'small' for the annotation lines; no numeric font sizes exist in the JSON.
Precise placement of the detection rectangles inside the two photos is described only relative to anatomy (ears, nose, blanket edge, chair edge); exact coordinates are not derivable from the JSON.
The yellow-highlighted blank in annotation line 2 presumably stands for the word 'Yellow', but the source shows a blank; it is reproduced as a blank, not filled in.
Hex values for photo content (blanket #8A9BA8, chair #5B3A1E, dog coat #C8B49A) are model estimates and cannot be verified from the JSON alone.
The two photographs are external assets: the checklist describes their content, but the actual image files must be sourced separately to reproduce the slide exactly.
